note: Presence is one answer per account and one lease per device, and nothing said how the second becomes the first. The contract required multi-device aggregation and named no rule, so two devices in different states produced whatever a reader assumed. The rule is stated here as a precedence over lease states and a projection onto the three audience values, and the validator evaluates it under both device orderings: a merge that depends on which device was read first is not a merge. Nothing executes it against a server, because no presence surface exists.

merge_rule.note: The account's availability is the projection of the most-present lease it holds. Precedence rather than recency, because recency needs a clock the devices do not share and would make the answer depend on which pulse landed last. `revoked` sits below `expired` and both project to offline, so a revoked device cannot pull the account's answer above what its remaining devices support. The account-level policy in profiles.presence_visibility is evaluated after this fold and can only narrow the result: a private participant reads offline to a viewer who is not authorized, which is the same value an inactive participant reads, so the suppression is not itself a signal.

cases.title: one active device and one expired device merge to online
cases.note: The case the fold exists for. Read desktop-first a naive last-write merge answers offline, and the participant disappears while still working.

cases.title: an idle device and an expired device merge to idle
cases.note: Idle outranks expired. An expired lease is an absence of evidence about that device, not evidence the account is gone.

cases.title: a revoked device does not raise the account answer
cases.note: Revocation is a security act. A revoked device contributing presence would let a device the participant removed keep reporting them present.

cases.title: three devices in three states merge to the most present
cases.note: The fold is over a set and not a pair, which is where an implementation written for two devices stops agreeing.

cases.title: every device expired merges to offline
cases.note: The negative case for the fold: no ordering of expired leases produces a present account.

cases.title: an account with no lease row at all merges to offline
cases.note: The other negative case. An empty device set must not fall through to a default that means present; `empty` is stated rather than left to whatever a fold over nothing returns.
